comparators.title: Using mass-balance principles to optimize nutrition of lettuce
comparators.authors: Noah James Langenfeld and Bruce Bugbee
comparators.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science, Volume 17, article 1885837

system.crop_or_subject: Three lettuce cultivars: Grand Rapids, Red Sails and Rex
system.system_type: Deep-water culture hydroponics; zero-discharge nutrient solution
system.setting: Research greenhouse, Utah State University, Logan, Utah, USA
system.duration: Study 1: 25 × 28-day crop cycles over 707 days; Study 2: 7 cycles over 196 days; Study 3: 9 cycles over 252 days
system.replication: Three cultivars; repeated crop cycles are not independent facilities
system.sample_basis: Solution volume maintained at ≥90% of initial 53 L; plant tissue nutrient analyses and daily EC measurement

reported_metrics.basis: Element-specific mass balance across the closed-system study
reported_metrics.notes: The article does not claim every element has >90% recovery.

reported_metrics.basis: No nutrient solution was discarded in the long-term zero-discharge studies
Study 1, 707 days; yield and nutrient uptake reported as consistent

reported_metrics.unit: g dry biomass per L transpired
reported_metrics.basis: Nutrient refill recipe design value for the stated conditions
reported_metrics.notes: Not a universal crop constant; depends on CO2, humidity, VPD and crop conditions.

reported_metrics.basis: Later zero-discharge study condition reported without yield advantage from replacing to 1.0 mS/cm

reported_metrics.value: approximately 5 ppm N, 1 ppm P, 10 ppm K
reported_metrics.unit: mg/L elemental basis as described by source
reported_metrics.basis: Stable low solution concentrations in the long-term experiment

limitations: Deep-water culture in one research greenhouse; not multi-facility or underground vertical-farm validation.
The approach depends on crop tissue composition, transpiration/growth relationship and stated environmental conditions.
The authors measured EC daily and used tissue analysis to establish or refine refill composition; this is not evidence that no monitoring or assays are ever needed.
The first study showed accumulation of some passive-uptake elements when refill composition was too concentrated.
The nutrient mass-balance study does not qualify microbial safety or food-safety release of a recirculating loop.
comparators.transferability: Strong longitudinal comparator for crop-specific nutrient mass balance and zero-discharge operation. Replicate on matched crops and source-water chemistry, then challenge salinity, cultivar transfer, changing VPD/CO2 and biosecurity.
comparators.claim_ceiling: Published controlled greenhouse DWC studies only. No general zero-discharge guarantee, no food-safety certification, no vertical-farm transfer claim.

reported_metrics.basis: Raw irrigation water used in study

comparators.venue: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture, article 110588

system.system_type: Greenhouse closed-loop hydroponics with ISE monitoring and variable-composition fertilizer replenishment
system.replication: The publication reports a crop trial; facility and independent-compartment count require full-method extraction

ISE measurements versus chemical analysis
ISE measurements versus chemical analysis

limitations: Only nitrate, K and Ca were measured by the described ISE array; not a complete trace-element profile.

comparators.title: Continuous recirculation of hydroponic-nutrient solutions shifts bacterial communities and induces plant-defense gene expression in lettuce
comparators.authors: Cora M. Kenderdine and Rosa E. Raudales
comparators.venue: Applied and Environmental Microbiology, Volume 92, Issue 4, e0164725

system.crop_or_subject: Lettuce cultivar Rex; Pythium myriotylum plant-pathogen treatment
system.system_type: Deep-water culture with reused autoclaved or non-autoclaved nutrient solutions, with/without P. myriotylum
system.replication: Study reports n=5 in plant-growth figures
system.sample_basis: 16S rRNA gene sequencing, qPCR detection of P. myriotylum, plant-defense gene expression

reported_metrics.basis: Bacterial community differences in nutrient solution across cycles
Bacterial community differences in roots across cycles
Community dissimilarity associated with P. myriotylum presence in nutrient solution
Community dissimilarity associated with P. myriotylum presence in roots

limitations: Plant pathogen and plant-defense study, not a human foodborne-pathogen survey.
Community shifts do not identify a universally beneficial or protective microbiome.

Edible-leaf sampling in the reported test

system.duration: Three environmental monitoring events over eight months

system.duration: Daily fertigation strategy through modelled crop cycle

reported_metrics.basis: Simulator compared with single-shot preparation baseline
Simulator compared with baseline
Simulator scenario results

limitations: Five simulator scenarios; not a measured crop or commercial facility result.

interpretation_rules: Do not interpret EC as elemental nutrient inventory; equal EC does not imply equal ion composition.
Retain chemical species and analytical basis; nitrate-N is not interchangeable with nitrate-ion mass.
A nutrient balance is not a food-safety balance. Chemical closure does not prove microbial safety.
A PCR-positive result does not automatically prove viable organism; a negative result does not prove facility absence. Preserve assay, viability status, matrix, detection limit and sampling coverage.
Do not classify all root-zone bacteria as harmful. Distinguish defined hazards, plant pathogens, indicators and beneficial/commensal microbiome evidence.
Nutrient or water recovery percentage is not a circularity or safety score; report product quality, treatment residuals, energy and crop suitability separately.
Zero-discharge claims must declare leaks, samples, purge, cleaning waste, filter residues, condensate and failed-batch disposal.
A model scenario or synthetic fixture cannot be promoted to measured crop/facility evidence.
No negative environmental sample, single reservoir assay or sanitation record independently certifies food safety or authorizes produce release.
Do not create cross-connections between root-zone solution, potable water, condensate, minewater/MTES and wastewater without qualified source, treatment and authority evidence.
claim_ceiling: Source-comparator registry only. It does not certify a hydroponic loop, water reuse, microbial safety, plant health, food release, discharge compliance or nutrient recovery process.
